LESSON: TRANS SAHARAN SLAVE TRADE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 3.3: Trans Saharan Slave Trade
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Trans Saharan Slave Trade, part of People and Relationships in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: where slaves were sourced during the Trans-Saharan slave trade. Why do people subject others to slave trade?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Trans Saharan Slave Trade together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Respect: Learners appreciate diverse opinions as they work together and discuss the effects of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa,

during the Trans-Saharan slave trade.

• Social cohesion: Learners work together amicably as they debate on factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave trade in

Africa.

Link to other Subjects:

• English and Kenyan Sign Language: learners use language skills as they discuss using signs, the effects of Trans-Saharan slave trade

in Africa.
